prompt:
Use case: product-mockup / premium fragrance campaign asset.
Create an ORIGINAL photorealistic commercial still-life photograph for ants, a fictional clean everyday soap-scent fragrance called FIRST LIGHT. It must look like an expertly lit real beauty campaign photograph, with physically convincing glass optics, sharp tactile detail and clean restrained art direction. Output a wide 16:9 landscape master image, at the highest available resolution; no website UI or poster copy.
Scene: an airy pale blue-white morning, a very shallow clear water surface with subtle organic sunlight caustics, a softly out-of-focus distant waterline, almost-white pale sky. The left 43% is quiet light negative space for later real webpage text. No geometric water grid, no oversaturated tropical water, no fog washing out the bottle.
Subject: ONE 50 mL perfume bottle centered around 72% of image width, fully visible from cap to base, occupying about 66% of the image height. A deliberately designed rounded rectangular heavy clear glass bottle, with defined optical edges, thick polished base, an actual visible internal cavity and very pale colorless-blue liquid filled to 78% with a delicate real meniscus. Modest narrow neck, thin satin-white collar and a finely shaded matte-white cylindrical cap, slightly narrower than the bottle, with precise gently rounded edges. The product is grounded on a barely submerged glasslike surface, with a soft real contact shadow and a restrained accurate reflection. No floating.
Optical craft: sculpted charcoal-blue edge reflections against bright whites, a large soft directional morning key light from upper left, slim rim highlights on the opposite edge, visible thick-glass refraction, clear distinction between glass, liquid, paper and matte cap. No plastic look, no flat translucent cube, no gray clay render, no rectangular pale flat panel.
Small physical water beads: only a few actual 1-3 mm clear condensation beads on the right glass shoulder and side, adhering to glass with surface tension and delicate highlights. No huge independent foreground water droplet, no egg shape, no bubble sculpture, no splashes.
Label: a small carefully proportioned matte ivory-white rectangular paper label with a very fine warm gray keyline. Typeset only these EXACT words, centered, elegant restrained contemporary sans serif: lowercase "ants" (a-n-t-s), beneath it smaller uppercase "FIRST LIGHT", and at bottom very small "50 mL". Crisp legible lettering, no invented text, no claims, no other logos. Match clean minimal branding, with enough breathing room on the label.
Camera: refined 85mm product photography, nearly front-facing with the right side subtly visible, straight verticals, depth of field keeps the complete bottle tack sharp while the distant surface is softened. Camera slightly above product mid-height. Elegant tonal depth, luminous whites and cool slate-blue edge contrast. Keep room around the bottle so it can be cropped responsively. The final image should convincingly establish a clean, desirable fragrance product. No people, flowers, shells, stones, towels, jewelry, ornament, typography outside the product label, watermark or border.
